result.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
result.summary: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. However, many existing red-teaming approaches rely on heuristics or impose strong assumptions that limit their applicability in fully black box settings. We address this gap by introducing $M^3$, an automated red-teaming framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP). In $M^3$, an attacker LLM interacts with a target LLM while operating over a compact internal state produced by a state LLM. Across two benchmarks and six target models, $M^3$ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art multi-turn red-teaming methods in Attack Success Rates (ASR), achieving improvements of up to 53% in ASR@5. Even with lightweight attacker, $M^3$ attains gains up to 26% in ASR@1 and 34% in ASR@5, compared to baselines that use higher capacity attackers. Beyond improved effectiveness, $M^3$ exhibits steeper risk escalation over conversational turns and achieves more consistent performance across risk categories (up to 4.82 improvement in Gini index) without relying on predefined risk taxonomy, providing a scalable and principled framework for multi-turn red-teaming and safety evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 将多轮越狱形式化为有限时域 MDP，由状态 LLM 把交互历史压缩成紧凑内部状态，攻击 LLM 据此与目标模型交互，并在两个基准、六个目标模型上以 ASR 等指标评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「显式紧凑状态 + 有限时域决策」可能与 LVR 中推理状态的压缩维护、轮次/长度扩展与停止决策建模有概念联系，可供核查；但工作本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
